# AmbientOS System Guide

AmbientOS is an AI-powered company orchestration platform where 8 autonomous agents run departments under human (CEO) governance. The system operates on a **propose -> approve -> execute -> audit** cycle, with a heartbeat that fires every hour (configurable in `function.json`, was 30 min before Claude Sonnet switch).


## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of the platform and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block._

### 2026-04-21
- **Keep-alive pinger shipped — cold starts eliminated.** GitHub Actions cron (`.github/workflows/keepalive.yml`, `*/5 * * * *`) hits new unauth read-only `/api/healthz` every 5 min, then POSTs the result to authenticated `/api/keepalive-record`. The record endpoint appends a `{ts, latencyMs, status}` entry to a 100-entry ring buffer at state key `pingLog` — written via `_utils/companyStorage.js` directly, bypassing `company-state/index.js` so no `VALID_KEYS` entry was added (`pingLog` is NOT a valid `company-state` API key, only readable/writable via the two new dedicated endpoints). Dashboard surfaces status via new authenticated `/api/keepalive-status` (null-safe on empty log) rendered as a `KEEPALIVE` pill in the CEO status strip on `modules/company/dashboard.html` alongside HEARTBEAT/API/DEPLOY/AI MODEL/BUDGET/FLEET — green <6m, yellow 6–15m, red >15m or `status=fail`. Verified post-deploy: healthz warm latency 79–127ms (target was <500ms), round-trip record→status works, first cron fire green. **Auth caveat:** the `x-company-secret` gate on record/status is currently a no-op because `COMPANY_WRITE_SECRET` env var is unset on the function app (same state as every other authenticated endpoint — `storage.validateSecret('')` returns `true` when the env var is empty). Ring buffer cap of 100 bounds the flood blast radius. No alerting in v1; failures surface in Actions tab. Discord/Slack webhook is phase 2 if real failures occur. Cost: zero (GHA cron inside existing minutes, ~8,640 extra function invocations/mo inside Azure consumption free tier).

### 2026-04-15 (later)
- **`activationMode` consolidated into `execution_mode`.** One autonomy dial now instead of two. `execution_mode` gained a `manual` value joining the existing `active | observe | frozen`: agents in manual mode propose + observe only, no task mutations, no memory writes. The redundant `activationMode` state key (which was never writable — not in VALID_KEYS — so always defaulted) has been fully removed: deleted `resolveActivationMode`, `_normalizeActivationMode`, `ALLOWED_MODES` from `helpers.js`/`constants.js`; swapped both manual-mode gate sites (task-mutation loop in `index.js`, remember handler in `agent-runner.js`) to check `executionMode === 'manual'`; collapsed the CEO Config dashboard's two-dropdown "Activation Mode + Automation Mode" panel into one "Execution Mode" dropdown with 4 values. Agent prompt GATE CHECKLIST rewritten to document `execution_mode` values. Experimental mode (the 1.5x rate-cap multiplier) retired — never wired in prod. Net: ~70 lines of dead code removed + simpler mental model.
- **Scribe prompt-size instrumented + cut.** Scribe was silently preflight-skipping every heartbeat at `agent-runner.js:398` (prompt >30K tokens → 0 actions, 2ms latency). Measurement via new `prompt-size` log event per agent per cycle (populates `ctx._sizeStats` in `buildHeartbeatPrompt` before return, `logEvent` at call site in `agent-runner.js`). Root cause: Scribe's 4 routed skills totaled 49,971 chars. Fix: dropped `storyforge` from Scribe's `SKILL_ROUTING` + hard-capped per-skill content at 12,000 chars (prevents the even-split trap where dropping a skill raised per-skill cap and nullified the win). Scribe now at ~28K tokens, actions resumed. `result.preflightSkipped` + `preflightEstimatedTokens` surfaced onto `perAgent` so future skips are visible, not silent.
- **Activation-mode log downgrade.** The bogus `policy-violation` with `gate: 'activation_mode'` that fired every heartbeat (missing state key → fell back to `supervised_autonomous` correctly but logged as a gate violation) is now a `run-health` entry in `logs`, not a governance violation. Consolidation above obsoletes this path entirely.

### 2026-04-14 (later⁴)
- **Emergence Monitoring shipped (new 15th system).** The platform gets an **immune system** watching compound patterns across all 14 prior systems. Five signals computed daily by new `emergenceCheckCron` (16:00 UTC, after memoryConsolidate at 15:00): (1) proposal rate per type per agent 7d/30d with YELLOW/RED thresholds, (2) reject rate per emitter 30d (CEO-resolved only, ≥5 samples required to prevent noise), (3) fleet churn velocity (approved `agent_*` proposals only, 30d, trend classified expanding/contracting/churning/stable), (4) capital RED streak length (bucket-by-day over heartbeatRuns), (5) approval queue depth + oldest-pending-age by blast-radius tier. **Pure observation layer** — monitor NEVER mutates state beyond `emergenceDigest` + `governanceLog` append. Forge sees an EMERGENCE SIGNALS prompt block (top 3 RED + top 3 YELLOW); CEO sees `/modules/company/emergence.html` with 7 sections including approval queue sorted by `EMERGENCE_BLAST_RADIUS` tier (critical→high→medium→low, `agent_retire_proposal` + `product_retire_proposal` + `agent_hire_proposal` = critical). Dedup across cron runs: same signal today as yesterday doesn't re-log; YELLOW→RED upgrade IS a new event. `_builtOnDemand: true` flag on fallback snapshots (stale >26h) surfaces as amber "live snapshot" banner. Design rule: "prevents meta-loop where monitoring system retires agents it thinks are runaway." Endpoint: `/api/emergenceMonitor` (GET, 26h freshness). Dashboard mirror of `EMERGENCE_BLAST_RADIUS` documented — if adding new proposal type, update both `constants.js` map AND `emergence.html` JS map. After System 15 the twirling tower has both a self-modification loop AND an immune system.
- **Agent Identity Evolution shipped (new 14th system).** The fleet itself is now mutable via proposal → CEO approval. Three new Forge-only action types: `propose-hire-agent` (cost ceiling $100), `propose-retire-agent` (protected agents can't be targeted), `propose-role-evolution` (shallow metadata only — focus / monthlyCap / doctrine / expectedActionMix; ceiling $50). `AGENT_IDS` + `AGENT_ROLES` are now loaded via bootstrap-fallback from new `agentRegistry` state key — inline defaults capture the original 8 as safety net; on first run they're written to state which becomes source-of-truth thereafter. Loader (`C.loadAgentRegistry(storage)`) called once at heartbeat start, mutates exported constants **in-place** so require-time destructure references stay valid. New `_EXEC_GROUPS` fallback: hired agents not in any hardcoded group get appended as a final sequential group so they execute. `PROTECTED_AGENTS = {nova, cipher}` cannot be retired (structural + functional roles). `FLEET_MIN_SIZE = 5`, `FLEET_MAX_SIZE = 12`, 14-day rejection cooldown. **Retire flow is atomic via idempotent write-order:** tasks reassignment (to `DOMAIN_LEAD_MAP[target]` with 'nova' fallback) → registry archive → governance log. CEO retry of approve is idempotent (state-check, not proposal-ID tracking — except evolve which uses doctrineHistory.proposalId). **Scope constraint (v1):** hardcoded prompt branches in prompt-builders.js (470+ lines of per-agent personality) remain unchanged — evolution mutates state-driven metadata only. Hired agents run immediately with template prompt; deeper personality requires deploy-time custom branch. Cohort arrays (`['cipher','forge','nova']` weekly-report, `['echo','scribe','quill']` content, etc.) also unchanged — hired agents graceful-degrade without cohort-specific behaviors until deploy. New endpoint `/api/fleetProposalCreate` (POST) for CEO direct proposal creation (bypasses Forge-only heartbeat gate — CEO is trusted authority). Extended `/api/approveProposal` handles both `product_*` and `agent_*` prefixes. New dashboard `/modules/company/fleet.html` (sidebar System → Fleet, admin-only, fa-users-gear) shows active roster with inline Evolve/Retire buttons, pending proposals with Approve/Reject, Forge's fleet intelligence readout (drift / cap-exceeding / stale), archived agents, recent decisions. Forge sees FLEET HEALTH prompt block surfacing drift candidates (from reflectionDigest.perAgent roleAdherence), cap-exceeding (from allocationDigest), stale (from financeDigest.agentEfficiency). Proposal suppression works by target — Forge won't re-emit what's already queued. Bootstrap verified LIVE at cycle-1776226816015: 8 agents auto-populated, `doctrineHistory: []` initialized, updatedAt stamped.
- **Goal Generation shipped (new 13th system).** Nova can now propose *product-level* lifecycle decisions — not just campaigns within existing products. Three new Nova-only action types: `propose-product` (new product launches, cost ceiling $100), `propose-pivot` (strategic repositioning of an existing product, ceiling $50), `propose-retire` (sunset a product, ceiling $10 — usually $0). Each proposal carries `estimatedCost` inline (no separate `request-budget` ceremony) and lands in `approvalQueue` as `product_proposal` / `product_pivot_proposal` / `product_retire_proposal`. `PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_AUTHORIZED_AGENTS = {nova}` (same pattern as `CAPITAL_AUTHORIZED_AGENTS`). Rate limit: 1/day per type per agent. Dedup: pending same-target blocks; 7-day cooldown (`PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_REJECT_COOLDOWN_DAYS`) on rejected same-target to prevent re-emit noise. Capital Allocation gate (shared with `propose-campaign`): blocks emission when system RED or squeezeMode ≥95%, unless Nova has a Cipher-approved budget decision in last 24h — fail-open on state-read errors. **Retire guard** logs a warning if target has >100 blog views 7d OR active campaigns and rationale doesn't acknowledge the live signal (prevents accidental retire on a live revenue source). **Nova's prompt** gets a new `PRODUCT LIFECYCLE` block (between allocation and cost sections) showing RETIRE candidates (DECLINING verdict + <2 posts 7d + flat/negative traffic), PIVOT candidates (STABLE + engagement.score <30 + research.activeCount ≥2), PENDING (suppresses already-proposed candidates to prevent token waste), and NEW PRODUCT CTA only when budget is healthy + no pending new proposal. Shape guard on `strategicDigest.perProduct` prevents silent degradation. New dashboard `/modules/company/goals.html` (sidebar System → Goals, fa-bullseye) with inline approve/reject via new `/api/approveProposal` endpoint (status flip + `resolvedAt` stamp; downstream side-effects like editing product-facts.json remain manual per v1). Rejections also append to `capitalAllocation.decisionLog` so the Allocation dashboard surfaces product rejections alongside budget rejections.
- **Capital Allocation shipped (new 12th system).** Cipher now has enforcement teeth, not just observability. Per-agent monthly LLM spend caps declared in `constants.js` AGENT_ROLES (`monthlyCap` field, summing to `FINANCE_BUDGET_MONTHLY=$15`: Scribe $4, Echo $3, Nova $2, Cipher/Pixel/Forge $1.50, Quill $1, Scout $0.50). New module `allocation-intel.js` builds `allocationDigest` composing month-filtered `geminiUsage` spend + `outcomeDigest` ROI retro + persisted `pendingRequests`/`decisionLog`. New state key `capitalAllocation` with automatic month rollover (archives to `history`, 12-month cap) + 100-entry FIFO `decisionLog`. **Two new action types:** `request-budget` (any agent; tiered routing: <$0.50 auto-approve unless squeeze mode or systemStatus=RED, $0.50-$2 → `pendingRequests.pending_cipher`, >$2 → `pending_ceo` + `approvalQueue` entry `kind: budget_request`) and `approve-budget-request` (Cipher-only via `CAPITAL_AUTHORIZED_AGENTS`, requires reasoning note, writes `auto:budget-rejected`/`auto:budget-approved` memory to requesting agent with `evidence.runId + requestId`). `propose-campaign` gate: blocks when agent is over-cap (status RED) or system in squeeze mode (≥95%), unless a request-budget was approved in last 24h — fail-open on state-read errors. **Prompt injection:** every agent sees `YOUR BUDGET` (cap/spent/remaining/status) + `SYSTEM BUDGET` (spent/budget/pct/status/squeezeMode) block between workspaceSection and costSection. Cipher additionally sees `PENDING BUDGET REQUESTS` + `RECENT BUDGET OUTCOMES` (variance retro). **ROI feedback loop:** experiment auto-conclude (Self-Awareness Phase 4b hook) stamps `actualCost` (sum of `geminiUsage.totalCost` for that agent between `startedAt` and `concludedAt`) + `costVariance`; appends `experiment-concluded` entry to `decisionLog`. New endpoint `/api/allocationDigest` (90-min on-demand fallback) feeds new dashboard `/modules/company/allocation.html` (sidebar under System → Allocation, fa-coins icon): 6 sections — hero, per-agent spend bars, pending requests, recent decisions, campaign ROI (proportional spend attribution — geminiUsage has no campaign_id so it splits system spend across engagement-producing campaigns), experiment ROI with variance %. Programmatic verification: `heartbeatRuns[-1].digestsBuilt.allocationDigest = true`.
- **Shared World Model shipped (new 11th system).** Every agent now sees a canonical `WORLD STATE` block at the TOP of their heartbeat prompt — identical text across all 8 agents, updated every heartbeat. Contains: company runway days, finance status (monthly spend %, burn trend, projected month-end), fleet (stalled agents), followers by platform, products with `launchedAt` + growth signals, active objectives + campaigns with pace, experiments summary, open approvals count + oldest age, recent material events (7d, ceo-reject + stall-alert + experiment-concluded + campaign_complete — excludes routine ceo-approval noise and campaign-pace-alert). New module `world-state-intel.js` is a pure aggregator — pulls from `financeDigest`, `forgeOpsDigest`, `outcomeDigest`, `strategicDigest`, `socialAccountStats`, `contentDigest`, and raw state; never recomputes. Single source of truth per field. Hard cap 1500 chars on the block — throws on overflow. Extracted `_computeCampaignPace` from `social-intel.js` as a pure helper so both the velocity block formatter AND world-state consume it without any formatter-in-aggregator coupling. Programmatic verification: `heartbeatRuns[-1].worldStateInjected = true` + `worldStateBlockLength: <=1500>` stamped per run. Endpoint `/api/worldState` + dashboard `/modules/company/world-state.html` render the snapshot visually (sidebar under System → World State). Product-facts.json gained `launchedAt` + `status` fields on all 7 products. Token cost: ~72K extra input tokens/day across 8 agents × 24 heartbeats ≈ $0.02/day at Sonnet 4.6 input pricing.
- **Self-Awareness / Reflection System shipped (new 10th system).** Every agent now gets a `YOUR SELF-REFLECTION` prompt block each heartbeat with deterministic fields: `coreQuestion` (from AGENT_ROLES doctrine), `decisionPatterns` (14d grouped by type with improved/tied/regressed/pending counts backfilled from `agentDecisions.outcome`), `strategyFatigue` (hook+platform clusters with ≥5 attempts AND median engagement <70% of agent median — requires outcome data), `roleAdherence` (actual 7d action mix compared to new `expectedActionMix` field in AGENT_ROLES, drift labels observational not punitive), `repeatedFailures` (tasks with 3+ failed_attempt comments). 3-day cadence nudge for ALL 8 agents (not just weekly-report cohort) — `lastReflectionAt: null` handled as 999-days-overdue so first-deploy nudge fires immediately. New L4 types: `reflection` (30d TTL) and `consolidated_belief` (90d TTL). New daily cron `memoryConsolidate` (15:00 UTC) collapses clusters of 5+ similar memories into a single consolidated_belief with evidence chain preserved — guards against <7d entries, protected sources (experiment-verdict, ceo-edit), max 3 consolidations/agent/day. Scout/Quill/Pixel get a `REFLECTION FOCUS` one-line prompt instead of empty data sections (their decision hooks don't fire — generic block was prompt noise). New dashboard at `/modules/company/awareness.html` (sidebar under System) with cadence grid, role-adherence table, fatigue signals, decision leaderboard, consolidation history. Sidebar badge lights when `reflectionsOverdue >= 3` OR `roleDriftCount >= 2` — fatigueSignalsCount excluded (steady-state noise across 8 agents). Rolling `runtimeMemory.reflectionDigestHistory` (last 5) enables drift-staleness detection — 3+ cycles with persistent drift surfaces "expectation review" chip on the agent card so CEO can decide whether the static baseline needs updating.
- **Outcome Attribution System shipped (new 9th system).** Every social publish now writes a `t0` baseline snapshot to `outcomeSnapshots`; a new `outcomeRefresh` cron (daily 14:00 UTC) pulls fresh engagement at `t1/t7/t30` lag boundaries from X (OAuth 1.0a), Bluesky (AT Protocol public), and Reddit (/api/info). LinkedIn + Facebook deferred — `outcomeDigest.totals.linkedinPendingCount` surfaces the blind spot. Auto-post + direct create-social-action paths inject `?utm_source=<platform>&utm_content=<actionId>` into ambientpixels.ai URLs so blog views + form submits attribute back to specific posts. New module `outcome-intel.js` builds per-agent / per-experiment / per-hook / per-campaign rollups consumed by prompt-builders (agents see `YOUR RECENT OUTCOMES` block) and Cipher's upgraded campaignROI (actual-engagement $/outcome with `source` badge, falls back to task-count proxy when no complete snapshots yet). Experiment auto-conclude hits 4 gates: `samples >= 10`, `>= 5 per arm`, `|effectSize| >= 0.15`, verdict in `{promote, discard}` — writes `auto:experiment-verdict` learning memory + flips `agentExperiments[x].status = 'concluded'`. Structured `agentDecisions` log with 30d/10K retention hooks at quality-gate-rewrite + experiment-start sites; `outcomeRefresh` backfills `decision.outcome` once linked action reaches t7. New dashboard at `/modules/company/attribution.html` (linked in sidebar under Content) renders totals, experiment table, agent scorecards, hook matrix, campaign funnel, cost per outcome — every panel carries an explicit empty-state message for the 7-day wait.
- **Governance audit trail filled in.** All 8 blocking gates (orphan, exact/fuzzy dup, task/research ceiling, social promo, campaign freeze variants) now write structured `policy-violation` entries to `governanceLog` with `details.gate` + `details.reason` — previously they only `console.log`'d, leaving the audit trail hollow (0 entries in 200 records pre-fix). Wired via existing `logEvent` helper in [`agent-runner.js`](ambientpixels/api/companyHeartbeat/agent-runner.js).
- **Self-Correction 10/10 patches shipped.** Quality-gate rejections write `auto:quality-gate` feedback memory + `policy-violation` log so agents see the specific Haiku issues in their next reflection callout (filter broadened to any `source.startsWith('auto:')`). Stall detection + system-directive creation now emit `stall-alert` / `system-directive-created` events to governanceLog. Forge's prompt upgraded from advisory to MANDATORY directive creation on any stalled agent (unless already directed in last 3 heartbeats or externally-blocked). New campaign-pace correction tracker: campaigns >=2 weeks at <50% of target pace auto-escalate via `campaign_pace_escalation` approvalQueue entry + `auto:campaign-pace` memory to Nova + `campaign-pace-alert` log (7-day re-escalation dedup).
- **Deprecated escalation types auto-pruned.** `overdue_escalation` and `stale_revision_escalation` (removed from writes per Apr 11) are now pruned from the approval queue regardless of age at [`index.js:~421`](ambientpixels/api/companyHeartbeat/index.js#L421), clearing ~21 lingering entries.

skills.content: # AmbientScore Development Skill AmbientScore is AmbientPixels' standalone AI website conversion audit product. Users enter a URL, get an instant 0-100 score with a letter grade, see 3 teaser findings for free, and can unlock the full report ($29 single / $89 3-pack). The product lives at `/ambientscore/` and is self-contained — its own CSS, JS, and API layer. ## Recent Changes _Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of AmbientScore and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._ - **2026-04-21 — Editorial redesign landed.** The whole product moved off the dark emerald SaaS look to a formal editorial / filed-audit register. New palette (cream paper `#F3EEE3`, ink `#1A1613`, red stamp `#8C2F1E`), three typefaces (Source Serif 4, Inter, JetBrains Mono), bordered scorecards with ghost frames, mono dimension codes (`D-01 · MSG.CLR` through `D-08 · RSK.REV`), black grading-scale panel, signature block. Applies to landing, report (paywall + full), strategy intake, confirm. No em dashes anywhere in user-visible strings. All `as-*` classes and DOM ids kept so scan / paywall / credits / intake logic is unchanged. ## Architecture Overview ### Frontend Pages | Page | File | Purpose | |------|------|---------| | Landing | `ambientscore/index.html` + `js/ambientscore.js` | URL input, free scan results, upgrade CTA | | Report | `ambientscore/report.html` + `js/report.js` | Full report viewer with paywall logic | | Strategy | `ambientscore/strategy.html` + `js/strategy.js` | Lead capture intake form | | Confirm | `ambientscore/confirm.html` | Slot booking confirmation | ### API Endpoints | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | |----------|--------|---------| | `/api/as-analyze` | POST | Core scan — accepts `{ url }` or `{ sessionId }` (payment verification) | | `/api/as-report` | GET | Report retrieval — `?id=`, returns teaser or full based on unlock status | | `/api/as-credits` | POST | Credit check (`action: "check"`) or redemption (`action: "redeem"`) | | `/api/as-confirm` | POST | Strategy session confirmation with HMAC validation | | `/api/formIntake` | POST | Shared intake — type `"ambientscore_strategy"` for strategy submissions | ### Library Modules (`api/_lib/ambientScore/`) | Module | Role | |--------|------| | `analyzer.js` | Pipeline orchestrator — scrape → extract → classify → evaluate → score → synthesize | | `scraper.js` | URL fetching with SSRF protection, cheerio HTML parsing | | `dimensions.js` | 8-dimension model definition, weight profiles by site type, scoring helpers | | `promptBuilder.js` | Gemini prompt templates for each pipeline stage | | `scorer.js` | Deterministic scoring — decompression curve (1→0, 5→60, 10→100) | | `reportRenderer.js` | HTML report template generation | | `creditUtils.js` | Pack credit ledger (purchase/redeem history per email hash) | | `stripeClient.js` | Stripe checkout creation, session verification, webhook signatures | | `emailSender.js` | Azure Communication Services email delivery | ## The 8-Dimension Scoring Model The scoring model is the intellectual core of the product. It lives in `dimensions.js` and drives everything from prompt construction to report rendering. ### Group A — Conversion Funnel (55% base weight) 1. **Messaging Clarity** (15%) — Headline clarity, value prop specificity, jargon avoidance, consistency 2. **CTA Strength** (15%) — Visibility, action language, value alignment, placement 3. **Funnel Friction** (15%) — Step count, cognitive load, form optimization, distractions 4. **Conversion Hierarchy** (10%) — Visual hierarchy, information flow, progressive disclosure ### Group B — Trust & Differentiation (45% base weight) 5. **Trust Signals** (15%) — Social proof quality, authority markers, risk reversal, transparency 6. **Differentiation** (10%) — Unique mechanism, competitor contrast, category ownership 7. **Audience Alignment** (10%) — Language match, pain point addressing, sophistication calibration 8. **Quick-Win Fixes** (10%) — Low-hanging fruit count, implementation ease Each dimension has 3-4 sub-criteria. Gemini scores each sub-criterion 1-10, then the decompression curve maps LLM scores to 0-100 (because LLMs compress scores toward 5-7, a raw 5 maps to 60, not 50). Weights are dynamic — `dimensions.js` has profiles for SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, content, media, local service, and agency site types. ### When modifying the scoring model - Adding a dimension: update `dimensions.js` (definition + weights for ALL site-type profiles), `promptBuilder.js` (evaluation prompts for the correct group), `scorer.js` (if weight math changes), and `reportRenderer.js` (display). - Changing weights: only touch `dimensions.js`. The scorer reads weights from there. - Changing the decompression curve: only touch `scorer.js`. The curve parameters are there. ## Analysis Pipeline (4 Stages) The pipeline in `analyzer.js` runs 4 Gemini calls (2 in parallel for Group A/B evaluation): **Stage 0 — Scraping** (`scraper.js`): Fetch URL, parse HTML with cheerio, extract headings, CTAs, forms, social proof, pricing, schema.org, body text. SSRF protection blocks localhost, private IPs, and cloud metadata endpoints. **Stage 1 — Extraction** (Gemini call #1): Parse scraped data into structured JSON — headlines, value props, CTAs, trust elements, audience signals, friction points, conversion paths. **Stage 1.5 — Classification** (Gemini call #2): Classify site type (SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, etc.) to select the right weight profile. **Stage 2 — Evaluation** (2 parallel Gemini calls): Group A and Group B dimensions each get their own call. Returns 1-10 scores per sub-criterion + reasoning + findings. **Stage 3 — Scoring & Synthesis** (`scorer.js`): Apply decompression curve, compute weighted score, generate priorities, headline/CTA rewrites, confidence level. ### Pipeline development rules - Gemini prompts live in `promptBuilder.js` — keep prompt changes isolated there, not in `analyzer.js`. - The analyzer orchestrates; it should not contain prompt text or scoring logic. - Rate limiting (5 free scans/hour per IP) is enforced in `as-analyze/index.js`, not in the library. - Report data is stored as `cc_report_` in Azure Blob via `company-state` API. ## Monetization & Credits ### Stripe Flow 1. User clicks "Unlock" → `ambientscore.js` calls `/api/as-analyze` with just `{ url }` initially for free scan 2. For paid unlock → Stripe Checkout session created in `as-analyze/index.js` via `stripeClient.js` 3. After payment → redirect back with `sessionId` → `as-analyze` verifies payment and unlocks report 4. 3-pack purchase: 1 credit auto-redeemed for triggering report, 2 remaining ### Credit Ledger - Storage key: `cc_credits_` in Azure Blob - `creditUtils.js` manages the ledger: purchase entries, redeem entries, balance calculation - Credits are checked/redeemed via `/api/as-credits` endpoint - Frontend stores credit state in `sessionStorage` under `cc_pack_credits` ## Design System (Editorial Audit Report) AmbientScore's register is a formal filed-audit / financial document, not a SaaS landing page. Every visual decision is deliberate. Do not mix in SaaS tropes (gradients, glow, emoji, cards-with-shadows). ### Color tokens | Token | Hex | Usage | |-------|-----|-------| | `--paper` | `#F3EEE3` | Primary background (cream paper) | | `--paper-2` | `#EAE3D3` | Secondary bg (stats strip, dimension grid) | | `--paper-warm` | `#FBF7EB` | Dimension cells, warm panels | | `--rule` | `#D4CBB5` | Hairline rules, dotted borders | | `--rule-2` | `#BDB299` | Slightly darker rule | | `--ink` | `#1A1613` | Primary text, rules, buttons, dark panel bg | | `--ink-soft` | `#3D342C` | Body copy on cream | | `--ink-muted` | `#6B6052` | Meta labels, captions | | `--stamp` | `#8C2F1E` | Red editorial accent. Use sparingly: corner stamp, eyebrow rules, `›` caret, dimension codes, section eyebrows | | `--steel` | `#BFB5A0` | Muted text on dark panel (grading scale) | Body has two subtle radial gradients layered on cream to feel like paper, not a flat fill. Do not remove. ### Typography Three families loaded from Google Fonts (`` in every page head): - **Source Serif 4** — all headlines, giant grade letter (224px on hero sample, 200px on live scorecard), scorecard score, section headers, signature - **Inter** — body UI, button labels, form inputs (15–16px, weight 500–600) - **JetBrains Mono** — dimension codes, eyebrow labels, meta, uppercase chrome (10–11px, letter-spacing 0.14–0.22em) ### Emphasis rules (CRITICAL) Only three marks of emphasis. Nothing else: 1. **Italic serif** — editorial emphasis in headlines (`audit`, `method.`) 2. **Red stamp** (`--stamp`) — only: corner stamps, eyebrow rules, 36×2px red rule above quiet CTA, `›` caret before signature, dimension codes, section eyebrows 3. **All-caps JetBrains Mono** — codes, meta, ranges **Do not invent new emphasis mechanics.** No underlines, highlights, drop shadows, or color accents on body text. The restraint is the design. **No em dashes anywhere in user-visible strings** — use periods, colons, or the `›` caret. ### CSS conventions - **Prefix**: `as-*` for all classes - **Self-contained**: `ambientscore.css` has no dependencies on AmbientPixels framework - **Responsive**: Desktop-first. Breakpoints at `960px` (stack hero / method / dim / sig grids, collapse form layouts) and `560px` (stack remaining grids, collapse url-forms, smaller hero) - **Print styles**: hero / CTA / loading / decorative sections hidden; white background - Search `ambientscore.css` before creating new classes — reuse what exists ### Dimension codes (display contract) The JS maps dimension labels to the editorial codes shown in the UI. Keep this map in sync when dimension labels change in `api/_lib/ambientScore/dimensions.js`: | Label | Code | Short | |-------|------|-------| | Messaging clarity | D-01 | MSG.CLR | | CTA strength | D-02 | CTA.STR | | Trust signals | D-03 | TRS.SIG | | Funnel friction | D-04 | FNL.FRC | | Social proof | D-05 | SOC.PRF | | Offer clarity | D-06 | OFR.CLR | | Content flow / Continuity / Conversion hierarchy | D-07 | CNT.FLW | | Risk reversal / Differentiation / Quick-win fixes | D-08 | RSK.REV | The map lives as `DIM_CODES` at the top of both `ambientscore.js` and `report.js` (duplicated; update both). ## JavaScript Conventions - **Pattern**: IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expressions) — no module bundler, no framework - **DOM**: Vanilla `document.querySelector` / `innerHTML` — no jQuery, no React - **Security**: All user-facing strings go through `escapeHtml()` utility - **State**: Module-scoped variables (`currentReportId`, `currentUrl`) — no global state - **Error handling**: User-friendly inline error messages, not console-only ## Storage Keys | Key Pattern | Contents | |-------------|----------| | `cc_report_` | Full report JSON (score, dimensions, findings, rewrites) | | `cc_ratelimit` | IP-based rate limit tracking | | `cc_analytics` | Scan event analytics (90-day retention, 10K cap) | | `cc_credits_` | Credit purchase/redeem ledger | These use the `company-state` API with `x-company-secret: pixelpusher` header. The `cc_` prefix is a legacy from ConversionCore — do not rename (backward compat). ## Email Integration - Provider: Azure Communication Services (ACS) - Sender: `DoNotReply@ambientpixels.ai` - Template in `emailSender.js` — self-contained HTML safe for all email clients - Triggered after report unlock — sends full report summary to purchaser's email ## Security Considerations - **SSRF**: `scraper.js` blocks private IPs, localhost, and cloud metadata URLs before fetching - **Rate limiting**: 5 free scans/hour per IP in `as-analyze/index.js` - **HMAC**: Strategy confirmation uses HMAC token validation - **Anti-spam**: Form intake has honeypot field, minimum time-to-submit (2.5s), rate limiting - **Stripe webhooks**: Signature verification in `stripeClient.js` - Never bypass these protections — if they're in the way during development, ask the user ## Common Development Tasks ### Adding a new dimension 1. Define in `dimensions.js`: name, description, sub-criteria, weight in ALL site-type profiles 2. Add evaluation prompt in `promptBuilder.js` (assign to Group A or B) 3. Update `reportRenderer.js` to display the new dimension 4. Verify `scorer.js` picks it up (it reads from `dimensions.js` dynamically) ### Modifying report output - Report HTML template: `reportRenderer.js` - Report viewer (frontend): `report.html` + `report.js` - Report data structure: created in `analyzer.js` Stage 3 ### Changing pricing Current prices: **$29 single / $89 3-pack**. Change in all of the following when they move: - **Stripe** — price IDs in `api/_lib/ambientScore/stripeClient.js` + Stripe dashboard - **Landing CTAs** — `ambientscore/index.html` hero pricing line ("$29 full report with rewrites"), the quiet-CTA subtext ("$29 for the full report"), the stats-strip line ("Twenty-nine dollars for the full report") — note the stats strip is written out as words - **Landing buttons** — `ambientscore/js/ambientscore.js` → `buildFindingCard` / handleBuy has `'Unlock full report . $29'` as the reset label for the buy button. The HTML also has `$29` / `$89` in button labels - **Paywall** — `ambientscore/js/report.js` paywall render: `'Unlock full report . $29'` - **Masthead sub** — `index.html` mast-sub line "Issued on demand . 60 seconds . $0 to $29" - **Credit pack size** — `api/_lib/ambientScore/creditUtils.js` ### Adding a new API endpoint - Create `api/as-/index.js` + `function.json` - Add route in `staticwebapp.config.json` if needed (but be careful — that file has high blast radius) - Follow existing patterns: `x-company-secret` header check, try/catch with 500 response, JSON body parsing ## Future: Claude Migration There's a standing plan to switch from Gemini to Claude API for the analysis pipeline (better reasoning, more nuanced observations). Not yet active — the user said "not now." When AmbientScore analysis quality comes up, this option is worth mentioning.

# Blindspot Game — Development Skill

Use this skill when working on the Blindspot game — a standalone arena combat game at `/blindspot/`. Blindspot is fully independent from CardForge as of Mar 21, 2026 — zero shared CSS, JS, images, or audio. APIs forked but card save remains shared (product-agnostic).

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of Blindspot and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

### 2026-05-07 — Publish-flow gap closed + public stats dashboard shipped (15 commits, range `c2489a676..89b56190d`)

Two distinct features shipped end-to-end. Read this whole entry before touching `bs-save-card.js`, `blindspot-quick-build.js` Step 5 (Become), `bs-battle-results.js` victory path, the `/api/blindspotstats` endpoint, the new `/blindspot/stats.html` page, the `/blindspot/admin/` Stats tab, or `imageEngine.appendToIndex`.

**Publish-flow gap closed** (commit `c2489a676`)
- Quick Build save now defaults `publishedToGallery: true` and fires `cardforgepublish` automatically after the user-blob save succeeds. Three pipelines all call into the same publish path: Quick Build (default-on toggle), Forge → Details (existing checkbox), Boss-1 nudge (new one-shot overlay).
- New publish toggle on Card Reveal screen (Step 5 "Become") — checked by default, copy: *"Show this card in the public gallery — Other players can browse it. You can change this later in Forge → Details."* Player can uncheck. State stored in module-scope `_publishOptIn` and passed into `BlindspotSaveCard.save(state, stats, wantsPublished)`.
- Guest-pre-auth flow: `bs-deck` localStorage now carries `publishedToGallery` per card so `persistPending()` (which fires when a guest signs in) honors the original choice. Defaults to `true` if missing on older deck entries.
- One-shot Boss-1 nudge: after the player's first `isNewBossDefeat`, a small Vein-themed overlay fires 2.2s after rewards: *"You're on the board. Show your card in the public gallery so other players can browse it."* with **Show in gallery** / **Maybe later** buttons. Direct API call on accept; sets `localStorage.bs-publish-prompt-shown = '1'` regardless of choice so it never repeats. Skipped if card already published, or if guest (no userId for `published-cards.json`).
- Why this matters: at deploy time the 7-player corpus had only 37 of 95 forged cards published (39%) — the AmbientOS Content Gallery showed 298 historical AI generations vs 37 published cards. The publish gap was real; default-on closes it for all future cards. Existing unpublished cards hit the Boss-1 nudge on their next new boss defeat.

**Public stats dashboard** (12 commits, range `481145066..89b56190d`)
- New endpoint **`GET /api/blindspotstats[?detail=admin]`** ([api/blindspotstats/index.js](ambientpixels/api/blindspotstats/index.js)). Aggregates 6 metrics from blob storage with a 10-min in-memory cache per Function instance. Returns `{ ok, asOf, stats: { players, cardsForged, cardsPublished, bossesDefeated, battlesFought, aiGenerations } }`.
  - `players` — count of profile blobs at `cardforge/blindspot/profiles/*.json` that successfully parsed (intentional: unreadable blobs don't inflate the player count).
  - `cardsForged` — sum of `arr.cards.length` across `cardforge/user/{userId}/cards.json`. Note: actual blob shape is `{ cards: [...] }`, NOT a top-level array.
  - `cardsPublished` — `parsed.publishedCards.length` from `cardforge/published-cards.json`. Note: actual key is `publishedCards`, NOT `cards`. Both fallbacks (top-level array, `parsed.cards`) supported defensively.
  - `bossesDefeated` — sum of `profile.highestBoss` across profiles.
  - `battlesFought` — sum of `profile.totalWins + pvpRecord.w + pvpRecord.l` across profiles.
  - `aiGenerations` — read from new counter blob `company-state/content-engine/total-count.json` (see counter section below).
- Cache strategy: module-level `_cache` with 10-min TTL. Cold-start instances re-aggregate once. Stale-cache fallback on errors — if aggregation throws AND there's a previous cached payload, serve it with `_stale: true` flag rather than 500. Preserves `_warning` field through the stale path so the operator never loses the "run backfill" hint.
- Admin gate: `?detail=admin` returns `adminExtras: { todayDelta, weekDelta, lastActivityAt, topPlayersByWins }` ONLY when caller's `x-ms-client-principal` decodes to a userId in `ADMIN_USER_IDS = ['5bb115c5-9077-4049-8af0-ce5085a9c315']` (mirrors `blindspotadminconfig`). Non-admin callers with `?detail=admin` get the public response silently — no 403, no leakage.
- Daily/weekly delta baselines stored at `blindspot/stats-baseline.json` with `{ dayStart: { asOf, stats }, weekStart: { asOf, stats } }`. Rolls forward at UTC date change (day) and approximate ISO-week boundary (week — uses `floor(dayOfYear/7)`, NOT true ISO 8601, drift is at most 1 day per year and explicitly accepted).
- 2N+4 blob ops per cache miss where N = player count (2 listings + N profile bodies + N user-cards bodies + 1 published-cards + 1 counter). At <500 players ~1000 ops, dollars and seconds. Will need heartbeat-precomputed `blindspot/stats-cache.json` if N crosses ~2000.

**AI-generation counter infrastructure** (commits `481145066`, `543a3c543`, `0244778b3`, `e7f25cbee`)
- New helper `bumpTotalGenerations(n)` in [imageEngine.js](ambientpixels/api/_lib/contentEngine/imageEngine.js) — read-modify-write of `company-state/content-engine/total-count.json` ({ count, updatedAt }). Called from `appendToIndex` on every successful image generation, with `n = entry.successCount || 1`. **NOT atomic** — JSDoc is honest about this. Concurrent generations may lose increments under contention; acceptable for a stats dashboard. Wrapped in try/catch at both the helper and call site so any failure stays best-effort and never breaks the calling generation flow.
- Why a separate counter: `content-engine/index.json` is hard-capped at 500 entries (see line ~531 in imageEngine.js). Its length cannot serve as a true historical count. The counter blob grows monotonically.
- Backfill script at [scripts/backfill-content-total-count.js](ambientpixels/scripts/backfill-content-total-count.js) — one-shot Node script the operator runs after deploy to seed the counter from historical `usage/YYYY/MM/usage_*.json` records. Uses `imagesGenerated` field from each usage record (falls back to 1 if missing, with `falledBack` counter so the operator can spot non-conforming records). **Aborts with exit 1 if it finds zero blobs** — refuses to silently overwrite the counter with 0 on misconfiguration. Idempotent: writes the absolute count, so re-running produces the same result.

**Public stats page** (commits `7f8006564`, `5bf812f1d`)
- Standalone Vein-themed page at `/blindspot/stats.html` ([stats.html](ambientpixels/blindspot/stats.html), [stats.css](ambientpixels/blindspot/stats.css), [stats.js](ambientpixels/blindspot/stats.js)). Single fetch on load, no auto-refresh. Renders 6 tiles in a 3×2 desktop grid (collapses 2×3 at 768px, 1×6 at 480px).
- Cinzel display + Share Tech Mono mono, ember gold accents on `--bs-bg` dark background. Uses CSS custom properties from `blindspot.css` with hex fallbacks so the page stays legible if `blindspot.css` fails to load.
- All `.bs-stats__*` selectors are scoped under `.bs-stats-page` (body class) because `blindspot.css` already has unscoped `.bs-stats__header` and `.bs-stats__title` rules for the in-game Stats screen. Without scoping they leak in and break the page header layout.
- `meta robots="noindex,nofollow"` set deliberately — the page is reachable only by direct URL in v1, and we don't want crawlers indexing it before the dashboard is verified working.
- `aria-live="assertive"` on the error paragraph so screen readers announce when JS reveals it. `aria-live="polite"` on the warning paragraph (`#bs-stats-warning`) which surfaces `data._warning` from the API.
- **No inbound links** in v1 from any product surface (splash, lobby topbar, Fighter Profile menu). Decision is deliberate — verify the dashboard works in production before wiring discovery. Revisit when ready.

**Admin Stats tab** (commits `168d7555f`, `6a32bf917`)
- New 5th tab in [`/blindspot/admin/`](ambientpixels/blindspot/admin/index.html) (Moderation / Hero / Hall / Gallery / **Stats**). Same 6 tiles as the public page plus admin extras: today/week deltas as colored chips (green for positive, neutral for zero, no `--down` modifier yet for negatives), last-activity row (relative time), top-5 players by wins (truncated 8-char userIds in mono).
- Lazy-loaded — `wireStatsLazyLoad()` uses MutationObserver on the panel's `[hidden]` attribute plus a click-handler fallback. `loaded` boolean guards against double-fire. Wiring lives inside `boot()` AFTER `SURFACES.forEach(renderSurfaceTab)` so the data fetch only happens once the auth-gated app is rendered.
- Delta chips use DOM construction (`createElement('strong')` + `textContent` + `createTextNode`) rather than `innerHTML` concat, so future `DELTA_KEYS` extensions can't introduce XSS via label strings.
- Admin styles namespaced as `.bs-admin-stats__*` — no collision with the `.bs-stats__*` classes used by the public page or the in-game Stats screen.

**Wiring + glue** (commit `c72ff61b0`)
- Static Web App route added to `staticwebapp.config.json` immediately after the `blindspotadminconfig` block: rewrites `/api/blindspotstats` to the Function App. As of deploy time this propagates separately from the Function App deploy and may take an extra SWA build cycle to land. Both clients use `buildApiPath('stats')` which resolves to the Function App's direct URL via `bs-config.js`, so the public page works regardless of SWA proxy state.
- `bs-config.js` registers `stats: 'blindspotstats'` in the `apiEndpoints` map.

**Smoke test** — extended from 32 → 37 checks. Added: stats.js parse (1e), blindspotstats/index.js parse (1f), stats.html tile hooks (5e), admin Stats tab hooks (5f), staticwebapp.config.json route (5g), bs-config.js endpoint registration (5h).

**Operator action required after deploy** — run the backfill once:
```powershell
$conn = az functionapp config appsettings list --name ambientpixels-nova-api --resource-group ambientpixelsV2 --query "[?name=='AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING'].value | [0]" -o tsv
$env:AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING = $conn
node ambientpixels/scripts/backfill-content-total-count.js
```
Then `az functionapp restart --name ambientpixels-nova-api --resource-group ambientpixelsV2` to clear the in-memory cache (the function may have aggregated `counterMissing: true` before the backfill wrote the blob; without restart the cache will serve stale `_warning` for up to 10 minutes). Already done at deploy time — the counter was seeded with 298 historical generations.

**Watch list / pitfalls**
- **`user/{userId}/cards.json` shape is `{ cards: [...] }`, NOT a top-level array.** Same for `published-cards.json` which uses `{ publishedCards: [...] }` (NOT `cards`). The endpoint reads both correctly post-`89b56190d`. If you ever re-shape these blobs, update the endpoint to match.
- **Cache TTL is 10 minutes per Function instance.** After any operator action that modifies storage (backfill, manual blob edit), restart the Function App to force fresh aggregation. Otherwise wait up to 10 minutes for the cache to expire.
- **`prefixBlobKey` is applied to counter + baseline reads but NOT to player-data reads.** This is intentional: `prefixBlobKey` is a `company-state` container demo-isolation helper. The `cardforge` container has no such mechanism. In production `BLOB_PREFIX` is unset so it's a no-op everywhere; the asymmetry only matters for staging/demo envs.
- **Counter is non-atomic.** Concurrent generations can lose increments. JSDoc says so explicitly. If you ever care about exact accuracy, lease the blob — but the dashboard tolerates drift.
- **`isoWeekKey` is `floor(dayOfYear/7)`, NOT true ISO 8601.** Function comment is honest. Drift at most 1 day per year on weekly delta resets. Don't "fix" without checking that the spec actually needs ISO-correctness.
- **Boss-1 nudge fires on `isNewBossDefeat`, NOT on Boss 1 specifically.** Stranger auto-credits Boss 1 via localStorage (per the 2026-03-31 fix), so for most players the nudge fires after their first lobby Boss 2 defeat. The "first time you win a real boss fight" wording is accurate for the player experience.
- **Default-on publish is opt-out by design.** Privacy-conscious players uncheck on the Card Reveal screen and never see their card in the public gallery. The toast copy is honest: *"Other players can browse it."* Don't change to opt-in without conscious decision — it would silently re-introduce the publish gap.
- **Quick Build's `_publishOptIn` resets to `true` only on `open()`.** Within a single wizard session (back/forward through steps) the player's choice persists. Don't reset on render.
- **The 6 stat keys are a contract.** `players / cardsForged / cardsPublished / bossesDefeated / battlesFought / aiGenerations` appear identically in: endpoint response, public page `data-value-for` attributes, admin tab `data-stat` attributes, smoke test required-strings list. Renaming any of them breaks all four surfaces.
- **No inbound links to `/blindspot/stats.html` deliberately.** When you decide to wire it in, candidate spots: splash footer KPI tile row ("View live stats →"), Fighter Profile dropdown menu ("Live Stats"), or as a 5th tile in the lobby Loot Zone. Pick one — three would clutter.
- **The publish toggle in Quick Build is the simpler write path.** Forge → Details checkbox is the "change my mind later" surface. Boss-1 nudge is the recovery path for cards that slipped through. Don't add a fourth surface.

### 2026-05-04 — Topbar rebuild + Fighter Profile + onboarding battle port (~25 commits, range `ed0399176..0f6cc97c8`)

Long autonomous session covering five distinct shipped pieces. Read this whole entry before touching `bs-auth-ui.js` (heavily rewritten), `bs-notifications.js` (new), `bs-profile-image.js` (new), the `.bs-topbar*` CSS block, the Fighter Profile section in `renderStatsScreen`, or the `#bs-battle-container` markup in `index.html`.

**Onboarding battle markup ported to Apr-27 redesign** (commits `ed0399176`, `235aa4e6b`)
- `index.html` `#bs-battle-container` was still using the pre-Apr-27 layout: top header bar with round + help + forfeit, HP/stamina bars as siblings outside the card frame, 2-section center column. Same `blindspot-battle.css` landed on that old DOM produced a "shorter, chromeless" Stranger fight that did not match the campaign battle look.
- Rebuilt to match `play.html` `#bs-screen-battle`: invisible round span, `arena-combatant__backdrop`, vertical HP/stamina rails INSIDE `.arena-combatant__frame`, item tray inside the frame, hidden meta wrappers, 3-zone center column with round pill / boss intent / matchup chip / flavor / hype meter / boss-stance indicator / stance row / utils cluster.
- Added `bs-boss-card.js` to the index.html script list (`ed0399176`) — Stranger's opponent is `bs-boss-1` (Gatekeeper) per `game-config.json`, so the boss card needs the mirrored render.
- Closed a 69px gap below the battle log (`235aa4e6b`) — `min-height: calc(100vh - 69px)` was subtracting topbar height in two places, but `index.html` deliberately has no topbar (Apr-30 splash redesign). Outer `#bs-battle-container.blindspot-battle` rule now uses `100vh`; inner `.arena-battle` rule got an override for `#bs-battle-container` only (play.html keeps the `- 69px` for its real topbar).

**Lobby New Card / Manage Deck duplicate fix** (commit `497e87b7b`)
- When the deck hit the 8-card cap, "Forge New (swap a card)" routed to the deck screen — same destination as Manage Deck, so the two buttons read as a duplicate. The "swap a card" label promised a forge that could not actually fire until you came back.
- `#bs-new-card-btn` now hides entirely when `deckSize >= MAX_DECK_SIZE`. Manage Deck is the single path. After retiring a card it re-appears as "+ New Card" and routes straight to Quick Build like normal. ([bs-card-switcher.js:113-123](ambientpixels/blindspot/js/lib/bs-card-switcher.js#L113))

**Topbar rebuild (6 phases, commits `63ad4fb0e` → `3591e5fe7`)** — replaces the old "5-element right-side chip pile" with a structured 56px bar.

Final composition (right to left):
```
[gold divider 1px @ 15% alpha bottom border]
[Blindspot brand]   ...   [Lv N pill] [🔥 N pill] [🔔(N) bell] [👤 Name ▾]
```

- **Phase 1: Bar geometry** (`63ad4fb0e`) — `.bs-topbar` height: 56px fixed, padding: 0 16px desktop / 0 12px mobile, `position: relative; z-index: 50`, gold divider at 15% alpha replaces the muted brown border.
- **Phase 2: Stats pills** (`acf063cb6`) — split fused stats chip into TWO independent `<button class="bs-topbar__pill">` (Level + Sparks) in an 8px-gap wrapper. Both are 32px tall with full-opacity gold border + low-alpha gold tint background. Click handlers in `bs-nav.js`: Sparks pill calls `showScreen('shop')` + `renderShop()`; Level pill currently shows a toast with current level + XP (TODO marker for the progression detail screen when one ships).
- **Phase 3: Notification bell + popover** (`c56401933`) — new `bs-notifications.js` (window.BsNotifications). Reads counts from THREE existing data sources, no fabricated notifications:
  - `BsRewards.getDailyBounties()` incomplete count
  - `BsCrates.getCrates()` length
  - `BsState.progress.asyncInboxCount`
  Badge shows total, hidden at 0, displays `99+` above 99. Popover panel (280px, glass bg, gold border @20%) anchored under the bell with one row per category. Inbox row navigates to PvP screen; bounty/crate rows return to lobby. `BsNotifications.refresh()` is called from `renderLobby()` so the badge stays current after every lobby render. Idempotent bind, outside-click + Esc close.
- **Phase 4: Fighter avatar trigger** (`521ba244e`) — replaced the generic `fa-user-check` icon in the user chip with a 24px circular portrait of the player's equipped fighter card. New `getSelectedCardFromCache()` reads `bs-deck` + `bs-selected-card-id` from localStorage (same source `guestGreetingName` already uses, no callback dependency on `blindspot-flow.js`). Falls back to `fa-user-shield` silhouette when no card. User chip resized 36px → 32px to match status pills.
- **Phase 5: Dropdown structure** (`f92bae8c1`) — replaced flat dropdown with structured menu: header strip (40px avatar + display-font name + meta line "LV N · X sparks"), main view sections (Admin / Fighter Profile / Settings / How to Play / Sign out), divider before destructive actions, Settings sub-view reachable via the Settings row. Settings sub-view has a Back button that reads as a header row. New `setView()` / `getActiveView()` helpers. Hierarchical Esc: on Settings view, Esc returns to main; on main, Esc closes and restores chip focus. Tab focus trap wraps focus inside the active view only.
- **Phase 6: Settings panel + audio off bar** (`3591e5fe7`) — removed `#arena-sfx-toggle` and `#arena-music-toggle` standalone speaker buttons from the topbar. Three new toggle rows in the Settings sub-view: Sound effects, Music, Reduce motion. Audio rows call `ArenaAudio.toggleSfx` / `toggleMusic` and sync the On/Off state pill from localStorage flags. Reduce motion label was renamed from "Reduce effects" but the storage key (`bs-reduce-effects`) and body class are unchanged for backwards compat.

**Fighter Profile system (5 phases, commits `ab6a1ba43` → `0f6cc97c8`)** — new player-identity surface, distinct from the equipped fighter card.

- **Phase A: Server data** (`ab6a1ba43`) — added `profileImage` (string) and `profileImageTransform` ({scale, posX, posY}) to the default profile. New `setProfileImage` POST action on `api/blindspotpro

# CardForge Development Reference

CardForge is a browser-based RPG card creator with 40M+ visual combinations, AI generation, deck building, and a public gallery. It's a **pure card creator** — the arena battle system was removed in April 2026 (Blindspot handles combat). It runs as a static frontend on Azure Static Web Apps with Azure Functions APIs and Azure Blob storage.

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of CardForge and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

### 2026-04-25 — My Forge dashboard (cardforge/forge.html)

Top-level entry point that surfaces a signed-in user's drafts, published cards, favorites, and decks (saved + published) on a single page, replacing the multi-step "open editor → open right sidebar → pick tab" navigation. Linked from the global nav as **Forge** between Decks and the auth chrome.

**Page:** [cardforge/forge.html](ambientpixels/cardforge/forge.html) — placeholder header (`<header data-cf-nav="forge"></header>`), hero, anon CTA, 2x2 panel grid (My Cards, My Published Cards, My Favorites — top row; My Decks wide panel — bottom row, splitting Saved + Published side-by-side).

**Orchestrator:** [cardforge-forge-page.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-forge-page.js) — `await window._cfPrincipalReady` (cached by cardforge-nav.js, no second `/.auth/me` round-trip), toggle anon CTA vs grid, mount/trigger panels.

**Reuse map:**
| Panel | How it mounts |
|---|---|
| My Cards (drafts) | `window.CardForgeMyCards.mount(container)` — new mountable module ([cardforge-my-cards.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-my-cards.js)) patterned on my-published-cards |
| My Published Cards | **Auto-binds** to `#cf-mpc-list` + hidden `<button class="forge-sidebar-tab" data-forge-tab="published">` proxy; orchestrator clicks the proxy on init to trigger lazy-load |
| My Favorites | Same auto-bind pattern via `#cf-fav-list` + hidden `data-forge-tab="favorites"` proxy |
| My Saved Decks | `window.CardForgeMySavedDecks.mount(#cf-msd-grid)` — pre-existing generic mount API |
| My Published Decks | `window.CardForgeMyPublishedDecks.mount(#cf-mpd-grid)` — pre-existing generic mount API |

**Critical pitfall — module mount API asymmetry:**
- `cardforge-my-saved-decks.js` and `cardforge-my-published-decks.js` expose **proper `mount(container)` APIs** — they're generic, drop-in.
- `cardforge-my-published-cards.js` and `cardforge-my-favorites.js` do **NOT** expose `mount()`. They auto-bind on DOMContentLoaded to hardcoded editor sidebar selectors (`#cf-mpc-list`, `.forge-sidebar-tab[data-forge-tab="published"]`, `.forge-tab-content[data-forge-content="published"].active`, etc.) and lazy-load on tab click.
- Forge page works around this by **mirroring the editor's selector skeleton** (hidden `<button class="forge-sidebar-tab">` proxies + `<div class="forge-tab-content active">` wrappers) so the modules find their elements, then JS-clicking the proxies in `cardforge-forge-page.js` to fire the lazy-load.
- **Don't refactor either card module without auditing both consumers** — editor sidebar AND forge page both rely on the auto-bind. If you give them a `mount()` API, retain backward compat or update both pages in lockstep.

**Page-specific CSS:** [cardforge-forge.css](ambientpixels/cardforge/css/cardforge-forge.css) holds page layout + brings forward the `.cf-mpc-row` / `.my-cards-empty` row styles (from cardforge-ui.css#5054, scoped under `.cf-forge`) so the page doesn't have to load the entire 5000+ line editor stylesheet just for four panels.

**CSS/asset dependencies on the page:** `cardforge-base` + card render chain (card / bg-effects / border-effects / glow-effects / icons) + `cardforge-ui-components` (forge-action-btn, mini-card-scaler, cf-mini-fallback) + `cardforge-splash` (nav chrome + global `.cf-nav-active` ember rule) + `cardforge-deck-builder` (db-mpd-grid + tile styles for the deck modules) + `cardforge-forge`.

**Editor sidebar deliberately unchanged.** Both surfaces co-exist; whether to slim the editor's right-sidebar tabs (My Cards / Published / Favorites / Deck Manager) is a follow-up decision once the dedicated page proves itself.

**`.cf-nav-active` rule moved from `cardforge-admin.css` → `cardforge-splash.css`** during this work so every page using the unified nav (gallery, decks, forge, faq, roadmap, admin, devlog) gets the ember active highlight, not just admin.

**Cache-bust suffix bumped to `v=20260425b` for cardforge-nav.js across all 8 consumer pages** (otherwise the new Forge link wouldn't surface until each page re-fetched the script). Splash CSS bumped to `v=20260425s` for the .cf-nav-active rule move.

**Editor exception — manual Forge link.** `editor.html` uses its own compact `cf-page-bar` (not the unified nav injector — the 3-col grid layout reserves only ~80px for the header), so it doesn't auto-pick up new entries from `LINKS` in cardforge-nav.js. The Forge link was added to `cf-page-bar__actions` by hand next to Decks, reusing the existing `cf-decks-link` class for styling. **When you add another nav slot to `LINKS`, remember to also patch `editor.html` manually** — it's the only consumer page that bypasses the injector.

**Subhead font pitfall (recurring).** `.cf-forge__sub` declared color/size but no `font-family`, and `body.cf-forge-page` had no font set either, so the subhead inherited the browser default and rendered in Times New Roman — same root cause as the deck.html nav font bug. Fixed by adding a `body.cf-forge-page` rule in `cardforge-forge.css` matching the splash body pattern (Inter + obsidian bg/text). Pattern to remember: **every new page-class body needs its own font-family rule** unless the page sits under `body.cf-splash`.

### 2026-04-25 — Auth-gated nav links (Decks + Forge hidden from anon)

Both Forge and Decks are now hidden from the nav for anonymous users. They render only when signed in.

**Reason:** Forge is 100% sign-in content (every panel needs a per-user collection). Decks looks public but [cardforge-deck-builder.js:451](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-deck-builder.js#L451) explicitly filters out default/sample cards, so a true first-time anon clicking Decks lands on an empty wasteland with zero cards. The shareable-deck-URL path (`?deck=<shareId>`) bypasses the nav, so this gate doesn't break sharing.

**Final nav state:**
| Anon | Signed in |
|---|---|
| Gallery / Editor / Sign in | Gallery / Decks / Forge / Editor / [user dropdown] |

**Implementation:**
- `requireAuth: true` flag on the Decks + Forge entries in the `LINKS` registry of [cardforge-nav.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-nav.js#L34).
- `renderLink()` adds `hidden` + `data-cf-require-auth` when `requireAuth && !readAuthHint()`.
- `readAuthHint()` reads `sessionStorage.cfAuthHint` synchronously — set by `loadPrincipal()` after `/.auth/me` confirms signed-in. **This is the FOUC fix:** any returning signed-in user paints the links visible on first frame because the hint persists across the session.
- The `loadPrincipal().then()` callback sets `gated[i].hidden = !signedIn` and writes/clears the hint accordingly.

**Editor cf-page-bar exception (manual):** editor.html doesn't use the unified nav injector, so the same gating was applied by hand:
- Tagged its Decks + Forge `<a>` elements with `data-cf-require-auth` + `hidden`.
- Added a small inline `<script>` immediately after `</header>` that reads `sessionStorage.cfAuthHint` synchronously and unhides for returning signed-in users (FOUC-free for the most common case).
- Extended the existing inline `checkAuth()` IIFE near the bottom of editor.html to flip the gated links + write/clear the same `cfAuthHint` based on `/.auth/me` truth.
- Pattern to remember: **whenever you add a new auth-gated nav slot, both `cardforge-nav.js LINKS` AND editor.html's inline IIFE need updating.**

**FOUC envelope:** the very first signed-in visit per session to ANY CardForge page does flash hidden→visible briefly because no hint exists yet. Every subsequent navigation in that session paints correctly. Acceptable trade-off; eliminating the first-flash would need either an HttpOnly-cookie-readable hint or a server-side render path.

### 2026-04-25 — Unified global header (cardforge-nav.js)

Single source of truth for the `cf-splash-nav` chrome across every CardForge page that uses it.

**Pattern:** any page drops `<header data-cf-nav="<active>"></header>` and loads `cardforge-nav.js`. The injector renders the canonical markup (brand → Gallery → Decks → Editor + auth-aware Sign in / avatar dropdown), highlights the active link, and wires the dropdown popover (click toggle + outside-click + Escape).

- `data-cf-nav` value (`gallery`, `decks`, `admin`, `faq`, `roadmap`, `devlog`, …) → applies `cf-nav-active` + `aria-current="page"` to the matching link.
- `data-cf-nav-extras="admin"` → renders the Admin link, hidden by default; flipped on after auth resolves IFF userId is in `ADMIN_USER_IDS`.
- Auth state cached at `window._cfPrincipal` + `window._cfPrincipalReady` (Promise) — other modules can `await window._cfPrincipalReady` instead of hitting `/.auth/me` again.
- Idempotent: re-mount is a no-op (sets `data-cf-nav-mounted="1"` on the header).

**Pages that use the placeholder:** index, gallery, admin, faq, roadmap, devlog, deck.

**Deliberate exceptions (do NOT convert):**
- `editor.html` keeps its `cf-page-bar` — compact bar fits the 3-col grid's 80px header height.
- `login.html` keeps the brand-only strip — no nav distractions during sign-in.

**Deck SPA refactor:** `cardforge-deck-builder.js`'s old `db-bar` brand + auth chrome was removed (was duplicated across 4 view modes). The global header now lives outside `#db-app` in deck.html so SPA re-renders below it don't disturb it. `db-bar` is now purely the deck builder's sub-nav (Builder / My Saved / My Published) + view-specific action buttons (Save, Publish, Copy Link, Clone).

**Devlog:** loads `cardforge-base.css` + `cardforge-splash.css` for the nav chrome while keeping `/css/base.css` + parent-site scripts for the body content (parent's `init-header-footer.js` still injects the footer at `#footer-container`).

**Pitfall — self-contained nav font:** the `.cf-splash-nav__links a` rule sets color/size/padding but NOT `font-family`. Splash, gallery, faq, roadmap have `body.cf-splash { font-family: Inter }` so links inherit Inter. Deck.html (and any future page that doesn't set body font) would inherit the browser default → **Times New Roman**. Fix: `.cf-splash-nav` itself now declares `font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif` so the nav is self-contained regardless of host page styling. Don't remove this without checking every consumer page.

**Files:** `cardforge/js/cardforge-nav.js` (~210 lines, idempotent IIFE). Removed duplicate `/.auth/me` + dropdown wiring from `cardforge-splash.js`, `cardforge-gallery-page.js`, `cardforge-admin-hero.js` (`renderNavAuth`), `cardforge-deck-builder.js` (`buildAuthMarkup` + `wireAuthBar`).

### 2026-04-25 — Admin KPI strip + favorites/hearts current state

**Admin KPI strip** (`api/cardforgeadminstats/` + `cardforge/admin.html` 4-tile grid):
- Admin-only `GET /api/cardforgeadminstats` returns `{ cardsPublished, users, hearts, favorites, computedAt, cacheAgeSeconds }`. 5-min in-memory cache per Function instance.
- Single enumeration over `user/` prefix yields Users (distinct prefixes) AND the favorites blob path list in one pass, then batches favorites downloads (50 in parallel). Hearts comes from summing `card-ratings.json`. Cards from `published-cards.json`.
- 4-tile responsive grid above the hero config form. `loadKpis()` is fire-and-forget from admin-hero init — KPI failure does NOT block the rest of the page.
- Auth: same `ADMIN_USER_IDS = ['5bb115c5-9077-4049-8af0-ce5085a9c315']` pattern as `cardforgeheroconfig`. Server gate is the source of truth (403 for non-admin). Endpoint accepts `x-ms-client-principal`, `x-cf-auth-principal`, or dev `X-User-ID` (non-prod only).
- Frontend uses `buildApiPath('adminStats')` (registered in `config.js apiEndpoints`). `setKpi(key, value)` applies `Number().toLocaleString()`.
- Phase 2 (deferred): weekly delta chips on each tile via `admin/stats-snapshots.json` written by a daily cron.

**Favorites system** — coupled with hearts, NOT separate endpoints:
- **Hybrid hearts:** anonymous users CAN heart (no idempotency, per-IP rate limit only — client tracks state in localStorage). Authenticated users get the "real" path: writing a heart also adds the card to their favorites blob, idempotent server-side.
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/cardforgerate` — body `{ cardId, action: 'add'|'remove' }`. Anonymous path increments aggregate count only. Auth path updates `user/{userId}/favorites.json` AND aggregate `card-ratings.json` together. Returns `{ cardId, count, hearted, idempotent? }`.
  - `GET /api/cardforgefavorites` — returns `{ cardIds: [], updatedAt }` for the authenticated user. Anonymous returns `{ cardIds: [] }` with status 200 (no 401 noise during boot).
  - `GET /api/cardforgeratings` — returns flattened `{ ratings: { cardId: count }, updatedAt }` for community display. 30s public cache.
- **Storage:**
  - `card-ratings.json` (root) — `{ ratings: { [cardId]: { count, updatedAt } }, updatedAt }`
  - `user/{userId}/favorites.json` — `{ cardIds: string[], version: 1, updatedAt }`
- **Caps:** `FAVORITES_HARD_CAP = 2000` per user. `add` past cap returns 409.
- **Frontend boot:** `CardForgeHearts.init()` is idempotent — call from any page that needs hearts/favorites state. Used by splash (highest-rated mode), gallery, and admin (KPI live preview).

**Auth flow (simple, current):**
1. Frontend calls `/.auth/me` (handles both `clientPrincipal` shapes — object or single-element array).
2. `window._cfGetAuthHeaders()` (in `config.js`) caches the principal and returns `{ 'X-CF-Auth-Principal': JSON.stringify(principal) }`.
3. Cross-origin POST/GET to `ambientpixels-nova-api.azurewebsites.net` go with `credentials: 'omit'` + that header (SWA does NOT proxy POSTs through `/api/*` rewrites — direct calls to the Function App are the canonical path).
4. Function `extractUserInfo(req, context)` reads, in order: `x-ms-client-principal` (SWA-injected, base64 JSON) → `x-cf-auth-principal` (custom forwarded JSON) → `x-ms-client-principal-id` → dev `X-User-ID` (non-prod only). Defaults to `{ userId: 'anonymous', isAuthenticated: false }`.
5. Admin gate is a hardcoded `ADMIN_USER_IDS` list inside each admin endpoint — NOT in SWA config. CSRF auto-injected on POST by `csrf-protection.js`.

**On deck — global header alignment:** the `cf-splash-nav` chrome (Gallery / Decks / Admin / Sign in / Open Editor) renders consistently on splash + gallery + admin, but other CardForge pages (editor, deck builder, login) still carry older nav variants. Next pass: factor a single header partial (or shared init that injects the nav) so every CardForge page gets identical chrome, active-link state, and auth-aware Sign in / user-status swap.

### 2026-04
- **Arena battle system removed.** CardForge is now a pure card creator. All arena endpoints, combat logic, and PvP references are gone. Blindspot handles combat as a standalone game. Do NOT reference arena features, battles, or PvP when writing about CardForge.

### 2026-04-24 — 3-panel obsidian redesign (massive)

The editor was rebuilt around a 3-column obsidian/ember design system. Big behavioral and structural changes — read this whole section before editing the editor or splash.

**Page split:**
- `cardforge/index.html` is now the **splash page** (hero card fan, 8-digit combo ticker, three ways-to-start tiles). Real cards loaded from `/api/cardforgeloadcards`. Empty fan until API resolves, then fade-in.
- `cardforge/editor.html` is the **editor** (formerly index.html). All script/link `?v=` cache-busts at `v=20260424i` after the redesign sprint.
- Splash → editor entry points: `?start=quick|preset|blank` (handled in cardforge-layout.js handleStartParam IIFE).

**3-column grid layout** (cardforge-layout.css):
```
.cf-app-grid: grid-template-columns: 220px minmax(520px, 1fr) 620px
              align-items: stretch; height: calc(100vh - 80px)
  .cf-rail        (col 1) — 12-entry workflow nav
  .cf-preview-pane (col 2) — card floats on obsidian background
  .cf-main-pane   (col 3) — controls (overflow-y: auto)
```
All three columns share a single row height. Rail can collapse to 64px via `body.cf-rail-collapsed`.

**12-entry rail nav with workflow groups** (editor.html):
- Groups: START / STYLE / CONTENT / SHIP
- Each `.step-btn` carries `data-nav-id` (string) + `data-target-section` (numeric) + optional `data-target-tier`. The numeric section maps to `[data-step-section="N"]` panes inside cf-main-pane.
- `data-target-section` 4 and 5 (buffs, attributes) live on the **back face** of the card; switching to those nav-ids auto-flips the card via `activate()`.

**CardForgeNav API** (cardforge-layout.js):
- `window.CardForgeNav.activate(btn, opts?)` — activates a rail button. `opts.suppressFlip: true` skips the auto-flip (used by click-to-edit on back-face zones).
- `window.CardForgeNav.activateById(id, opts?)` — same, by `data-nav-id`.

- Zone selectors include front classes (`.card-name`, `.card-stats`, `.card-badges` etc) AND back classes (`.badges-container`, `.attributes-container`, `.biography-section`, `.back-header`, `.bio-read-more`).
- When `e.target.closest('.card-back')` is truthy, handler calls `activateById(id, { suppressFlip: true })` so the card stays on the back while the rail jumps to the appropriate editor.
- A vestigial doc-level handler in `card-forge-editor.js` `initCardFlip` is now guarded with `if (step === null) return;` — the new rail doesn't carry `data-step`, and without the guard every rail click clobbered `flipped` to false.

| Token | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--cf-ob-bg-0/1/2/3` | Surface tones (deepest → lightest panel) |
| `--cf-ob-line-1/2` | Hairline divider colors |
| `--cf-ob-ember` `-soft` `-dim` `-22` `-33` | Ember accent + alpha steps |

| `--cf-ob-radius-md/-lg` | Corner radii |

Legacy tokens are **re-routed** to obsidian in cardforge-base.css — `--aura-bg-color`, `--aura-bg-secondary`, `--aura-glow`, `--mood-text-primary`, `--mood-secondary-color`, `--card-bg-primary`, `--dark-bg`, `--dark-text`, `--cf-text-muted` all alias obsidian values. **Do not introduce new raw hex/rgba** — use obsidian tokens.

**Card stats — no more combat stats:**
- `card.combatStats` (str/agi/int/end/lck), the fixed combat stat picker, `arena-combat-stats` block, and all wiring are **removed**. Card payload no longer carries a `combatStats` field. Severed from Blindspot deliberately — Blindspot still references `card.combatStats.*` (~25 refs in `blindspot-flow.js` + `api/blindspotasyncbattle/`); that path now reads cosmetic stats from the user-authored `stats[]` array (or its own internal model).
